ev.q: During 2001–2021, age-adjusted suicide rates involving firearms, suffocation, and other methods generally increased, and those involving poisoning decreased.
Deaths per 100,000 population are age-adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population.
Firearm-related suicide had the highest rates during the period.
Deaths per 100,000 population are age-adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population.
Suicides were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision codes U03, X60–X84, and Y87.0.
Rates of firearm-related suicide were stable from 2001 (5.9 deaths per 100,000 population) to 2006 (5.5), and then increased through 2021 (7.5).
